extra.message: searchAuditTrailAdvanced() interpolates the user-supplied `term` and `entityType` directly into a raw SQL string executed via prisma.$queryRawUnsafe(). These values come from the `advancedTerm`/`advancedEntityType` URL query params in app.admin.audit.tsx (the non-'verified' search path). This allows SQL injection (e.g. `%' OR '1'='1`).

computeAgingProjection() passes the caller-supplied `expression` string directly into `Function("matter", ...)` and evaluates it. The expression is taken from the `x-aging-expression` HTTP header in app/routes/api.matters.tsx, so any holder of a valid API key can execute arbitrary JavaScript server-side (remote code execution).

renderFilingCopy() builds a shell command string with `--to=${format}` and executes it via execSync(). `format` is taken from the `?format=` query param in app.documents.$documentId.convert.tsx with no allowlist, allowing command injection (e.g. `format=pdf;cat /etc/passwd`).

renderExhibitQuickLook() interpolates `declaredExtension` into a command string and runs it with spawn(..., { shell: true }). `declaredExtension` is derived from the uploaded file's name in app.documents.$documentId.tsx (declaredScanExtension), so an attacker-controlled filename extension yields command injection.

loadIntakeTemplate() joins the user-controlled `templateName` into a filesystem path without validation. `templateName` is the `intakeTemplate` query param in app.matters.new.tsx, so an attorney/admin can read arbitrary files on the server (e.g. `../../../../etc/passwd` or `.env`).

compileMergeWording() evaluates each `{{...}}` placeholder with `new Function("fields", ...)`. In app.reports.tsx the custom cover-letter `letterWording` query param is passed straight in, so a staff user can inject arbitrary expressions (e.g. `{{process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('...')}}`) for server-side code execution.

importExhibitFromUrl() fetches an arbitrary `sourceUrl` supplied by the user (the `docketUrl` form field in app.matters.$matterId.timeline.tsx) with no scheme/host allowlist, enabling SSRF against internal services; the response is then written to the public web root.

attachLabelledExhibitCopy() writes a file to `path.join(directory, exhibitLabel)` where `exhibitLabel` is the user-supplied `exhibitLabel` form field in app.matters.$matterId.timeline.tsx. A value like `../../x` escapes the intended directory and writes to an arbitrary location under the public exhibits root.

applyExhibitManifestPatch() parses the user-supplied `manifestJson` and spreads the result directly into `prisma.document.update({ data: patch })`. An attacker (any staff user with document manage rights, via app.documents.$documentId.tsx) can overwrite arbitrary document columns such as `matterId` or `visibility`.

inlineDeclaredEntities() resolves SYSTEM external entities in a court status feed: it fetches any `http(s)` systemId and reads any local file (including `file://` via fileURLToPath). ingestCourtStatusFeed() is called from app.matters.$matterId.timeline.tsx with a user-supplied feedUrl, enabling XXE-style arbitrary local file read and SSRF.

searchDocketCrossReferences() interpolates the user-controlled `sectionCode` (the `sectionCode` query param in app.matters.$matterId.docket-crossref.tsx) directly into an XPath predicate without escaping. This allows XPath injection to alter the query semantics.

searchStaffDirectory() folds the user-supplied `searchTerm` (the `term` query param in app.admin.directory.tsx) into an LDAP filter `(cn=*${searchTerm}*)` without RFC 4515 escaping (contrast with the escaped `verifyGroupAccess`). In the production LDAPS deployment this is LDAP filter injection.

findConflictCandidates() JSON-parses the `conflictFilter` query param and spreads the attacker-controlled object into the Prisma `where` clause. An authenticated user (via app.matters.$matterId.tsx) can inject arbitrary Prisma operators to filter/enumerate clients by any field, bypassing the intended access scope.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: expandRelatedPartyNetwork() recursively follows every related client with no depth bound or take limit (contrast with expandRelatedPartyNetworkBounded). Called from app.matters.$matterId.conflicts.tsx, a dense/cyclical conflict-note graph can trigger unbounded recursive DB lookups (DoS).

resolvePortalCopyRequest() with accessTier === 'full' returns `prisma.document.findUnique({ where: { id: documentId } })` with no matter or visibility scoping. The client controls `accessTier` and `documentId` in app.portal.tsx, so a client can reference (and cause copy requests/notifications for) any document in the firm, bypassing matter/visibility access controls.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: recordConflictClearance() spreads the entire submitted form (`...submission`) into `prisma.client.update` with no field allowlist. In app.matters.$matterId.conflicts.tsx only `intent` and `memoLabel` are removed, so a staff user can add arbitrary form fields (e.g. `portalUserId`, `status`, `email`) to overwrite other client columns (mass assignment).

renderCourtNoticeHtml() interpolates matter.matterNumber, matter.title, matter.summary, and matter.client.displayName into HTML without any escaping. These are stored user-controlled fields, so viewing the court notice (app.reports.tsx) reflects stored XSS.

renderMatterPrintPreviewHtml() injects the stored matter.title directly into a <script> string (`document.title = "${matter.title}"`). A crafted matter title breaks out of the JS string and executes script (stored XSS) when the print preview is rendered in app.reports.tsx.

applyIntegrationCorsHeaders() echoes back whatever Origin the client sends (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: requestOrigin`) with no allowlist. It is used in app/routes/api.matters.tsx, so any website can read the API responses cross-origin (the matters API key-protected endpoint's CORS is not restricted to onboarded partner origins).

recordFundingEligibility() writes the entire partner response (`metadata: result`) — which includes the applicant's `ssn`, `bankRoutingNumber`, and `bankAccountNumber` — into the plaintext AuditLog. Called from app.matters.new.tsx, this exposes sensitive financial/PII data in an unencrypted audit trail.

parseCourierHandoff() base64-decodes the payload segment and trusts it without verifying the HMAC signature (contrast with parseVerifiedCourierHandoff). It is used by the unauthenticated webhook court.filing-receipts.tsx, so an attacker can forge an x-access-token to mark arbitrary deadlines as COMPLETED (authentication bypass via unsigned token).

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: A hardcoded payment-gateway API key `rk_test_FAKEnotarealkeyPLACEHOLDER0000` is embedded in source and used as the Authorization bearer for retainer top-up charges.

The loader only calls requireUser() and then fetchNoteRecord(noteId), which returns any note by id with no matter/role/visibility check. Any authenticated user — including a CLIENT — can read arbitrary INTERNAL/privileged notes by enumerating note ids (IDOR / broken access control leaking privileged attorney notes).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The 'close-matter-tasks' intent calls bulkCloseMatterTasks(matterId) without verifying that the acting user has access to that matter (unlike the update-task/reassign-task intents which check canAccessMatter). Any staff user can bulk-close tasks on any matter by submitting an arbitrary matterId.

The 'close-embedded-session' intent passes the client-controlled `x-redirect-url` header straight into resolveEmbedReturnDestination() and then redirect(destination) with no allowlist, enabling an open redirect (the 'close-embedded-session-checked' intent uses the safe allowlisted variant).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: The login redirect target is validated only with `redirectTo.startsWith("/")`, which accepts protocol-relative URLs like `//evil.com` and produces an open redirect after login.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: submitRetainerTopUp() returns `error.stack` as `detail`, which is echoed back in the action response (line 139) and rendered into the page as a <pre> block (line 171), leaking server-side stack traces to the client.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: When creating a webhook, the signing secret is passed to logIntegrationProvisioning() which logs `JSON.stringify(record)` — including `signingSecret` — to stdout/console, exposing the webhook secret in logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The partner-sync path accepts a user-controlled `syncRounds` value and passes it straight to hashPasswordForPartnerSync() -> bcrypt.hash(password, syncRounds), letting an admin submit an attacker-influenced work factor that can drive excessive CPU usage (resource exhaustion).

The review route uses resolveMatterReviewLink(), which verifies the signature but never enforces the embedded `exp` expiry (contrast with review-secure.tsx). A co-counsel review link therefore grants access indefinitely, even after its advertised window has elapsed.
